_comment: Config for `mimo-code` — opencode driven by the mimo endpoint. Baked into
the image at /opt/claude-desk/ and pointed at by OPENCODE_CONFIG, never
under /home/claude: docker seeds a named volume only while it is empty, so
a file placed in the home volume never reaches an already-deployed desk.
{env:...} is opencode's own substitution — the key stays in .env.
permission: everything allowed, same bargain as `claude
--dangerously-skip-permissions` here. The container is the cage (no docker
socket, /work is the only mount from outside) and a per-tool tap on a phone
makes the desk unusable.
reasoningEffort (camelCase) is the key that reaches the wire as
reasoning_effort: verified by pointing the harness at a local echo
server and reading the body opencode actually sent. The snake_case
spelling is accepted by the config and silently dropped, which would
have left every turn on the default effort and looked like mimo being
slow. It is not a saving, it is the working setting: the
default burned 10,457 tokens/161s against 3,796/79s for a worse answer, and
mimo's wall time tracks the tokens it thinks (~30 tok/s).
limit.output is generous on purpose: opencode sends it as max_tokens
(seen in the captured body), and a small cap is spent on thinking first
so the turn comes back empty (shared/mimo.py).
instructions: opencode reads AGENTS.md, Claude Code reads CLAUDE.md —
this points the harness at the same house rules entrypoint.sh drops in
/work, instead of keeping a second copy that drifts.
